intents.definition: Establish that a declared compound operation settles after an injected between-effect failure only in the declared fully committed or fully uncommitted state, never the declared partial state.

distinctions.explanation: This intent excludes partial state for a compound operation after an injected between-effect failure; failure settlement and cleanup establishes terminal failure and cleanup completion without an all-or-nothing state guarantee.

intents.definition: Establish that a refused failed attempt does not consume or alter the declared legitimate authority and that a later valid attempt can still succeed with it.

distinctions.explanation: This intent preserves reusable authority across a failed attempt; refusal-before-effects instead constrains protected effects before refusal.

intents.definition: Establish that one unauthorized attempt is refused before it writes or mutates any member of the complete declared protected-effect population.

distinctions.explanation: This intent constrains protected effects before refusal; failed-attempt nonconsumption instead preserves reusable authority and its later usability.

This intent fixes an unauthorized attempt ending in refusal and excludes protected effects before that refusal; bounded-interval nonmutation fixes one actor and explicit interval endpoints without requiring refusal.

intents.definition: Establish in one exact captured graph that a closed canonical caller-input policy exactly partitions typed structural members; an exhaustive allowed-only request selects no coordinate and is accepted; an exhaustive authority-bearing request is refused; member-to-coordinate-to-operation-to-effect and request-through-cut identities are exact; the policy-derived source census is complete; and the forbidden attempt has no prohibited pre-refusal occurrence.

distinctions.explanation: This intent derives the closed input partition, both request surfaces, and resolution/source joins; refusal-before-effects starts from an already selected attempt and effect population. It supplies no identity or evidence here.

This intent proves the closed input partition, two parser outcomes, resolution chains, and refusal cut; forbidden-operation noninvocation prohibits a complete declared operation population for one subject and context but proves neither required incumbent use nor this input-boundary evidence.
This intent classifies exhaustive request members and binds acceptance and refusal; result-shape conformance checks one returned result's members and count. It supplies no identity or evidence here.

This intent owns policy, request, resolution, parser-outcome, and source-census identity in one graph; sound-negative observation proves one target absent from captured sources. It supplies no identity or evidence here.

intents.definition: Establish that every member of a complete declared consumer population applies one revoked authority state before every complete declared post-revocation attempt population and refuses those attempts without protected effects.
Establish that cancelling one declared generation reaches its cancelled state without changing the selected resource or authority of another generation, whose distinct attempt later succeeds.
Establish equal complete typed-observable populations, counts, and one explicitly paired canonical value across baseline and candidate behavior reports whose exact captured bytes are equal.

distinctions.explanation: This intent compares complete baseline and candidate behavior reports; integration-prefix safety quantifies over integration prefixes, execution paths, and required branches.

This intent compares baseline and candidate behavior reports and exact captured bytes; cross-representation parity compares two complete representations of one logical source without a baseline-to-candidate preservation claim.

intents.definition: Establish that a compact result plus its complete disclosed omission population reconstructs the complete source population and that the documented complete result equals that source population.

distinctions.explanation: This intent establishes complete-source recoverability across compact and complete modes; shape conformance establishes membership in one declared result schema.
This intent reconstructs one complete source from a compact result and disclosed omissions; parity compares two complete representations of one logical source.

intents.definition: Establish that exactly two overlapping attempts elect one accepted winner producing the sole declared effect and one rejected loser producing none while both observe the same durable resource state.
Establish that one authored design unit binds implementation and test loci, a complete nonempty requirement population, an exact warning shape, matching validation coverage, and zero placeholders.
Establish that a directly constructible component is inactive by default, has no activation events, and is unreachable from every declared production entrypoint in exact captured artifacts.
Establish that cleanup after one failed attempt settles without changing the declared independent protected resource or interfering with a distinct successful attempt.

Establish that exactly one failed attempt is cleaned up and settled with zero declared residue before one later retry of the same operation and input succeeds with exactly one declared final effect and the expected selected durable state.

distinctions.explanation: This intent binds exactly one failed attempt, residue-free cleanup and settlement, and one later successful retry with one final effect; idempotency instead compares one resource's complete observed state across two completed sequential invocations.

intents.definition: Establish that a declared failed attempt reaches its declared terminal settlement and completes its declared cleanup obligations.

distinctions.explanation: This intent establishes terminal failure and cleanup completion; atomic failure boundary instead excludes a declared partial state for a compound operation after an injected between-effect failure.

intents.definition: Establish that two completed sequential invocations with the same input leave one elected durable effect resource in equal complete observed state after the first invocation, immediately before the second, and after the second.
discovery_terms: state before and after second invocation

distinctions.explanation: This intent compares one resource's complete observed state across two completed sequential invocations; retry convergence instead binds one failure, residue-free cleanup and settlement, and one later success with one final effect.

This intent requires two completed sequential invocations and equal observed resource state; single-use replay refusal requires a state-changing successful first use followed by explicit refusal and unchanged state on one later replay.

intents.definition: Establish the declared required behavior for every mechanically materialized integration prefix, execution path, and required branch from exact captured integration inputs.

distinctions.explanation: This intent quantifies over integration prefixes, execution paths, and required branches; behavioral preservation compares complete baseline and candidate reports.

intents.definition: Without asserting terminality, establish that every member of the complete nonempty declared observation population strictly inside the bounded interval reads the same subject and records its selected baseline state, with the complete observed-state population equal to the complete singleton baseline-state population.

Establish that a complete nonempty observation population after one terminal event and before one bounded horizon records the terminal state at every observation, with an empty complete declared in-horizon reactivation-event population.
discovery_terms: after terminal event before bounded horizon

intents.definition: Establish that a declared observation after durable settlement sees the declared settled state.
Establish exact isolation of the selected ownership identity and its protected resources from a distinct owner or execution.
Establish that ownership handoff is fenced so the prior owner cannot perform the declared protected action after the successor acquires ownership.
Establish that the declared readiness condition is reached before the declared success event or result.
Establish that one complete observed result population contains every required typed member, only allowed members, no forbidden members, and an allowed shape with the exact emitted count.

distinctions.explanation: This intent checks one result against its declared allowed shape; lossless projection checks complete-source recoverability across compact and complete modes.

intents.definition: Establish equal complete typed-member populations, counts, and one explicitly paired canonical value across two complete representations of one logical source.

distinctions.explanation: This intent compares two complete representations; lossless projection reconstructs a complete source from a compact result and disclosed omissions.
This intent compares two complete representations of one logical source; behavioral preservation compares baseline and candidate behavior reports and binds their exact captured bytes.

intents.definition: Establish that a first authorized single-use attempt succeeds once and that a later replay is refused without another elected effect or resource-state change.

distinctions.explanation: This intent requires a state-changing successful first use and explicit refusal with no declared replay effect and unchanged resource state on one later replay; idempotency instead requires two completed sequential invocations whose three complete observed resource states are equal.

intents.definition: Establish that one declared actor neither writes nor mutates any member of a complete exact protected-resource population during one declared bounded interval.

distinctions.explanation: This intent fixes one actor and explicit interval endpoints and excludes mutation throughout that interval; refusal-before-effects fixes an unauthorized attempt ending in refusal and excludes protected effects before refusal.

intents.definition: Establish that one declared subject operation does not use any member of a complete exact nonempty forbidden-operation population in one declared execution context. This prohibition alone does not demonstrate use of a required incumbent implementation.

distinctions.explanation: This intent prohibits one complete declared operation population for a selected subject and context without proving required incumbent use; dormancy nonactivation establishes that a constructible component is inactive and unreachable from complete captured production entrypoints.

This intent prohibits every member of a complete declared operation population for one subject and context but proves no required incumbent use; bounded-interval nonmutation prohibits one actor's writes and mutations to protected resources between explicit interval endpoints.

intents.definition: Establish nonmutation of a complete declared protected-effect population within an explicit bounded interval, using either an unauthorized-attempt-before-refusal proof shape or an actor-and-interval nonmutation proof shape.

distinctions.explanation: This broader intent leaves the interval proof shape unresolved; refusal-before-effects fixes it to an unauthorized attempt ending in refusal.
This broader intent leaves the interval proof shape unresolved; bounded-interval nonmutation fixes it to one actor and explicit start/end events.

intents.definition: Establish, for exact captured input, complete result, ordering policy, and item-key/comparator evidence, exact population equality and deterministic total lexicographic order under at least two typed precedence keys and one stable tie-breaker, including complete pair coverage and input, declaration, and equivalent-serialization permutation invariance.

distinctions.explanation: This intent retains its own exact population spine and additionally establishes comparator policy, total lexicographic order, and permutation invariance; result-shape conformance does not mechanically unify population identities across a separate pack evaluation.

This intent checks one complete ordered result against a typed comparator policy and complete pair evidence; cross-representation parity compares two unordered representation populations and one paired canonical value.

intents.definition: Establish mutation-consistent pagination under one explicitly selected policy: immutable snapshot traversal or fail-closed stale versioned-cursor refusal.

distinctions.explanation: This intent prevents mutation-induced version mixing or requires fail-closed stale-cursor refusal; integration-prefix safety quantifies over integration prefixes.

This intent selects either immutable snapshot traversal or a self-contained stale-version refusal proof; refusal-before-effects alone does not bind page returns, cursor advancement, source versions, or the unrelated-mutation control.

intents.definition: Establish that one exact package-authenticated authoritative ordered-occurrence population is traversed from the canonical initial state through one linear opaque cursor chain under one snapshot/version identity, with exactly one terminal page and concatenated returned occurrences equal to the authoritative sequence exactly.

distinctions.explanation: This intent proves authenticated complete ordered traversal, once-only occurrence membership, linear cursor transitions, and terminal uniqueness; mutation-consistent pagination selects snapshot consistency or stale-cursor refusal without establishing full traversal completeness.

intents.definition: Establish absence of one exact captured target relative to one complete declared captured source population by proving complete source and observation coverage, stable endpoint pairs, authenticated per-occurrence target/source/attempt/position grounding, universal target non-match, an empty invalidating-condition population, and the sole exact projected absent conclusion.
discovery_terms: every observation does not match target

distinctions.explanation: This intent quantifies over complete declared source and observation populations and derives absence; direct-source authentication provenance proves one occurrence's target, source, and attempt provenance but not absence.

This intent establishes absence of a selected target relative to complete exact captured observations; dormancy nonactivation establishes inactive and unreachable component state from captured production entrypoints.

This intent uses stable endpoint pairs to validate captured source outcomes and then proves target non-match; bounded-state stability establishes that all complete nonempty declared observations strictly inside the interval read the same subject and record its baseline state, without terminality or an absence conclusion.

intents.definition: Establish that one exact caller-asserted boundary observation record is arithmetically and disposition-table consistent with one exact closed declared policy and exact captured boundary subjects, without claiming execution provenance or production enforcement.

distinctions.explanation: This intent validates a caller-asserted boundary record against captured policy and subject bytes; guidance propagation validates one authored guidance artifact and does not entail boundary-record consistency.

intents.definition: Establish that one exact raw guidance artifact carries exactly one nonconflicting plain-decimal value and exact unit token for every key in one exact closed declared policy.

distinctions.explanation: This intent validates one authored guidance artifact against the captured policy; boundary-record consistency validates caller-asserted boundary dispositions and does not entail guidance propagation.

intents.definition: Establish that one exact directly captured evidence occurrence authenticates one exact target, originates from the target's singular authenticated source of record, and was observed in one exact bound attempt.

Establish within one exact captured attempt that a valid settled core survives a later supplementary failure unchanged and complete, no supplementary result was produced, and the final result discloses exactly one captured reason while representing the failed component in exactly one closed present-unavailable or omitted-disclosed form.

distinctions.explanation: This intent binds one exact core settlement, later supplementary failure, final core preservation, no supplementary result, and exact disclosure; failure settlement and cleanup does not establish preservation of a successful core across a distinct supplementary failure.

This intent derives sub-result preservation and supplementary absence inside one exact attempt; behavioral preservation compares complete baseline and candidate reports and does not establish the supplementary failure lifecycle.

intents.definition: Establish for one exact selected test that authenticated evidence binds its candidate/snapshot, contract, obligation, target, binding, proof, and evaluator; the test is discovered, executed, passing, and not skipped; every declared falsifier is detected and every required traversal is proven, with no prohibited shortcut. No baseline inventory participates; sibling tests do not affect credit. Complete negative evidence is false, missing evidence/evaluator is not executable, and invalid evidence is refused.
discovery_terms: false not executable or refused evidence

distinctions.explanation: Implementation readiness binds design, test loci, requirements, warning shape, and placeholder absence; it does not authenticate or execute the selected test, detect its declared falsifiers, or prove its required traversal.

Behavioral preservation compares complete baseline and candidate reports; it does not establish the selected test's authenticated binding, passing unskipped execution, declared-falsifier detection, or required traversal.

Forbidden-operation noninvocation prohibits a complete declared operation population for one subject and context but establishes neither required incumbent use nor selected-test execution, falsifier detection, or traversal validity.
